input.quote: Such audit shall not occur more than [***] in a given Calendar Year, unless for cause, and shall not concern books and records relating to a period more than [***] preceding the current Calendar Year.
input.rationale: Section 9.9 lets each Party (including RevMed as against Sanofi) audit the other's financial books and records, so the rule is engaged notwithstanding mutuality. The clause fails the fallback on material terms: the frequency figure is a blank ([***] in a given Calendar Year) and is subject to an open-ended for-cause exception, so there is no effective annual cap; the notice floor is blank ([***] prior notice); and the cost-shift trigger is blank ([***] percent underpayment), leaving the auditing Party's cost obligation unquantified. Our edit states the cap in express operative language (audits shall occur no more than once per Calendar Year, with the for-cause escape deleted), sets fifteen days' prior notice, and fixes the cost-shift trigger at ten percent. Two preferred points are already met and left untouched: an independent auditor of international prominence (9.9(a)) who must sign a confidentiality agreement with the audited Party (9.9(d)). Business hours, off-site conduct and no-systems-access are preferred-only and not pressed, since the right reaches only books and records maintained under Section 9.8. Section 5.8 record review and Section 6.9 (Sanofi auditing RevMed) are not usage audits against us and are not flagged.

proposal.summary: Cap audits at no more than once per Calendar Year, require 15 days' notice, and set a 10% underpayment cost-shift threshold
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We set the audit parameters at our fallback position: no more than once per Calendar Year (deleting the open-ended for-cause exception that would defeat the annual cap), at least fifteen days' prior notice, and cost-shifting only where the underpayment exceeds ten percent. The limits remain reciprocal.

ops.oldText: which underpayment was more than [***] percent

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
